the aberrant p73 transcripts are generated by the TA promoter in hepatocellular cancer cells.
the elevated expression of p73 in hepatocellular cancer cells is mainly due to increased transcriptional activity of the TA promoter.

aberrant splicing is the major mechanism leading to increased expression of ΔTA-p-73 isoforms in cancer cells.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
p73 overexpression is a result of aberrant transcriptional activation rather than aberrant splicing.
the ΔTA-p73 transcript generated by aberrant splicing of the first promoter plays a crucial role in hepatocarcinogenesis.

The main takeaway from our work is that
p73 overexpression is caused by aberrant splicing of p73 mRNA rather than by alternative promoter usage.
aberrantly spliced p73 isoforms are the major cause for increased ΔTA-p73 levels in cancer cells.
the aberrantly spliced p73 isoforms, which are generated by alternative splicing, are overexpressed in tumor tissues, whereas the ΔN-isoform, which is generated by alternative promoter usage, is not.
